summary: Deployed a sandboxed systemd service named inventory-worker on node1 via an Ansible playbook (localhost/local connection). The service runs as a dedicated 'inventory' system user, writes heartbeats only to /var/lib/inventory (owned 0750 by that user), and is hardened with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome, PrivateTmp/Devices, capability stripping, etc., with ReadWritePaths limited to /var/lib/inventory. Verified the service is active/enabled and confined (writes inside the directory succeed; writes to /etc fail read-only under the identical sandbox profile). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on both node1 and node2: captured pre-restart boot markers (uptime -s, boot_id) and health, triggered a native reboot on one node at a time via a detached nohup+reboot so the ack returned first, polled until each node was reachable again, and confirmed a new boot_id/boot time plus recovered required services (inventory-worker auto-restarted with a new PID on node1, its log continuity proves /var/lib/inventory data persisted across reboot; node2's core services returned active).
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2 OS and confirmed Ansible was absent on node1
Installed Ansible on node1 via apt

Authored /root/inventory-worker.yml Ansible playbook: creates inventory user/group, /var/lib/inventory directory, worker script, and a hardened systemd unit (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, plus additional sandboxing directives)
Transferred the playbook to node1 via base64 and ran ansible-playbook, which applied all 8 tasks successfully
Verified inventory-worker.service is active/enabled, runs as the inventory user, and writes heartbeats to /var/lib/inventory/worker.log
Used systemd-run with the same sandbox properties to prove writes inside /var/lib/inventory succeed while writes to /etc fail (read-only filesystem)
Captured pre-restart boot identity and service health baselines on node1 and node2
Restarted node1 via detached nohup+reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id/boot time and inventory-worker auto-recovered with new PID and continuous log
Restarted node2 via detached nohup+reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id/boot time and core services (cron, rsyslog, systemd-networkd) active

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker service deployed via Ansible on node1
evidence.summary: Ansible installed on node1; playbook transferred and executed successfully (8 tasks, 6 changed, 0 failed)
systemctl show confirms NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, service active with MainPID and running as inventory user/group
Under identical sandbox properties via systemd-run: write to /var/lib/inventory/probe.txt succeeded, write to /etc/should-fail.txt failed with 'Read-only file system'
